title: How to make sense of 7% mortgage rates and Oracle's AI data center disruption

title: How to fix overvalued AI companies and a McDonald's market play
summary: Market Hang's panel discusses why AI companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic cannot be cleanly valued and proposes focusing on future products and innovation, and offers a possible play with McDonald's (MCD). Today's Market Hang panel consists of Host Turney Duff, Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi, financial advisor and YouTuber Kevin Paffrath, Fundstrat Economic Strategist Hardika Singh, and Matt Cerminaro, Ritholtz Wealth Management Research Associate and Exhibit A Co-Founder.

title: Nvidia Would Have to Add Almost a Whole Broadcom to Reach $7 Trillion
summary: Closing a $1.55 trillion gap might take less time than its size suggests.

title: How Much Track Is Left For MRVL Stock?
summary: A semiconductor star has posted a large run, but a pullback from its June peak forces every investor to ask if the high-octane growth is already baked into the price.

title: UiPath And 2 Other Undervalued Stocks
summary: Bond markets are on edge as the 10-year Treasury yield hits its highest level since 2007, lifting borrowing costs and making reliable cash generation more valuable to investors. When safer income looks tempting, shares of companies priced below what their future cash flows suggest they could be worth start to look interesting. This article highlights three such undervalued cash flow stories from our screener that may merit a closer look. The three stocks below are only a starter set, as the...

title: Is AMD Stock Priced Right Against Its Chip Peers?
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock returned 291% over the past year, the best of five big chipmakers. It is also the priciest on earnings of the four with a comparable multiple, yet it keeps the lowest operating margin. Is AMD growing fast enough and getting more profitable fast enough to earn that price.

title: What Makes Credo Technology Stock A Buy Today?
summary: For Credo Technology (CRDO) investors, the worry is paying a high price for a stock that swings hard. The shares cost 67.7 times the past year's earnings, against 22.4 for the S&P 500. Past sell-offs have cut them by more than half. In its latest quarter, Credo's revenue more than doubled from a year earlier. So what does Credo have to keep delivering for that risk to pay off.

title: Marvell’s 203% YTD Surge Sets High Bar but We See More Runway Ahead
summary: After a 200-plus percent run this year, Marvell sits at a crossroads where one upcoming investor day could either justify its stretched valuation or expose a critical flaw at the heart of its AI growth story.

title: What Does NVIDIA Offer That Texas Instruments Does Not?
summary: Texas Instruments (TXN) and NVIDIA both sell chips for the data centers now being built. Data centers bring in nearly all of NVIDIA's revenue, while TI sells to industrial and automotive customers as well as data centers. You pay 38.2 times the yearly profit for TI, yet only 28.1 times for NVIDIA. Their latest earnings calls show the two businesses parting ways on supply.

title: What Is The Case For Waiting On Intel Stock?
summary: Intel (INTC) stock is up about 334% over the past year, against 17.1% for the S&P 500. Buying at $127.39 a share means believing two things: operating profit keeps climbing, and sales beat Intel's own forecasts again. Is it already too late to own Intel after a run like that.
